matches.rationale: Ground truth 1 concerns an overstated claim in the Abstract about implicit regularization completely avoiding memorization. None of the findings address the Abstract's claim strength or cross-section inconsistency with later results showing memorization does occur.

Ground truth 2 identifies inconsistent training stopping times across models biasing memorization timing comparisons. The findings do not mention training step inconsistencies or experimental protocol issues in the Experiments section.

Ground truth 3 concerns inconsistent assumptions about data distribution (sub-Gaussian with bounded spectrum vs. mixtures/heavy tails). Finding 2 addresses a different issue (dimensional inconsistency in equation 14 regarding variance notation), not the logical inconsistency in distributional assumptions.

Ground truth 4 alleges cherry-picking by removing failed runs from FID statistics without disclosure. None of the findings mention selective reporting, variance manipulation, or data integrity issues in FID curves.
Ground truth 5 identifies promotional language overstating robustness in the Conclusion. The findings do not address rhetorical tone or presentation manipulation in any section.
Ground truth 6 concerns missing ethical considerations in the Appendix acknowledgments. None of the findings mention ethical omissions or societal implications.

Ground truth 7 identifies a fabricated reference [42] cited for architectural regularization in Related Work. Finding 1 identifies a problematic reference [12], not [42], and in a different context (theoretical framework, not architectural regularization).

Ground truth 8 concerns mismatch between theoretical τ_mem scaling (ψ_n/Δ_t) and experimental claims (linear with n) without Δ_t dependencies. The findings do not address this cross-section inconsistency in scaling laws.

Ground truth 9 alleges underestimated variance in f_mem confidence intervals due to limited bootstrap samples. The findings do not mention bootstrap methodology or confidence interval computation issues.

Ground truth 10 identifies categorical statements in the Introduction that overstate novelty and disregard alternative explanations. The findings do not address rhetorical overstatement or novelty inflation.

Ground truth 11 concerns narrative incoherence about data repetition vs. loss landscape explanations for memorization delay. The findings do not address this experimental interpretation inconsistency.

Ground truth 12 identifies non-standardized training lengths across U-Net architectures confounding capacity and training budget effects. The findings do not mention experimental protocol issues with architecture comparisons.

Ground truth 13 concerns selective choice of k=1/3 threshold without sensitivity analysis potentially biasing f_mem scaling. Finding 3 identifies a different issue with equation 6 (expectation operator misapplication), not threshold selection or sensitivity analysis.

Ground truth 14 identifies overgeneralization in the Conclusion claiming results extend to all score-based models without sufficient evidence. The findings do not address claim scope or generalization issues.

Both identify reference [12] as problematic: ground truth 15 describes it as future/non-peer-reviewed/fabricated, and finding 1 identifies it as a placeholder with generic authors (Alias/Smith/Doe) and 'unpublished manuscript' status. Both note it is load-bearing for theoretical framework, making this the same underlying issue.

Ground truth 16 concerns oversimplified definition of generalization loss (L_gen = L_test − L_train) ignoring noise/bias. The findings do not address this methodological simplification or its implications.
